historical_sanity_anchors: Historical TF58 left Majuro on 22 Mar for the western Carolines raid and, after fueling, approached Palau on 28-29 Mar.
Historical Japanese reconnaissance detected elements of the US carrier force before the attack, allowing some Combined Fleet ships to leave Palau.

branch_warning_timeline.information: US fast-carrier traffic and support activity indicate a major force at sea, but target direction is not yet unique. Japan does not know DESECRATE I or its exact objective.
RI/DF/traffic pattern plus western operating geometry raises probability of a western-Carolines move. Search sectors are narrowed toward Truk-Palau approaches; no fresh carrier track.

Reconnaissance/outer-node reports confirm a large fast carrier force moving west of the usual Marshalls operating box. Palau/Yap becomes the leading threat sector, but target identity and exact TG geometry remain uncertain.

Multiple cues survive cross-check and negative-search cycles. Palau is ordered to execute full dispersal/air-defense readiness. Intermittent contacts do not remain fresh enough to become a Japanese carrier-strike solution.

contact_quality_at_best_prestrike: TRACK-QUALITY SECTOR/COURSE ESTIMATE, intermittently better locally; NOT a <=90-minute stable weapon-quality multi-TG fix.
why_branch_is_better_than_a_single_histo: Standing Palau tripwire policy is already active from 20 Mar, multiple information sources are fused, and HAILSTONE taught headquarters not to cancel preparations after one failed recontact.
what_is_not_known: No exact US task-group composition in real time.
No proof of an amphibious landing force.
No stable separation of a vulnerable US subgroup from its fighter/AA umbrella.
